page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded capabilities alongside moderate multi-core and memory constraints. The instance achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core (2319.0) and text processing (2868.0) workloads, as well as strong single-threaded gzip compression (35.15 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.87 GB/sec). However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations show limitations. The multi-core stress-ng CPU performance (4094.67) and Passmark CPU score (6532.16) are categorized as weak, while the Passmark memory score (1085.12) is poor, reflecting a low memory bandwidth of 38.47 GB/sec for large block reads.

Given its high single-core performance but constrained memory capacity and bandwidth, the c4-highcpu-4 is best suited for compute-bound, single-threaded tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic text processing. It handles Redis SET operations at an average rate of 6.25 million operations per second and static web serving at 8.75 GB/sec. While it supports AMX instructions, LLM inference is limited, managing 38.26 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B model but dropping to a poor 4.86 tokens per second for text generation. The instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints or high multi-threaded concurrency.
